## Agent review preface (P2a agent pass)

**What this file is.** A mechanical candidate-grouping pass over the ~2,497 working labels captured across all 70 Phase-1 batches. Every group below is a *hypothesis that two or more labels might be worth looking at together in P3*, generated purely from surface signals (explicit agent hedges, shared notation/alias strings, lexical overlap, co-occurrence in the same contribution row). **No group is, or implies, an identity claim** (R5/R12). Nothing here has been merged, renamed, or resolved. A label sitting in ten groups is not "more real" than a label in zero groups — it only means more surface signal touched it, which is itself sometimes an artifact of a busy naming convention (see the SHARED-NOTATION note below) rather than of genuine relatedness.

**How to read the six signal types, after this agent's spot-check (see "Agent review notes" at the end of this file):**

1. **POSSIBLY-RELATION (650 groups) — trust as originally rated (STRONGEST).** Every group spot-checked against `11-OBJECT-INDEX.jsonl`/`11-UNRESOLVED-CANDIDATES.jsonl` reproduced the underlying row's `relation_to_existing`/`candidate_of`/`note` fields accurately. This is a human-in-the-loop-equivalent signal: an extraction agent, reading the actual source text, explicitly flagged the uncertainty at capture time. Still not identity — P3 still has to look — but the highest-value list for P3 to start with.
2. **UNKNOWN-CANDIDATE-GROUP (60 groups) — trust as originally rated (STRONG).** Same character as POSSIBLY-RELATION: an agent looked at a specific piece of evidence and explicitly named the candidate objects it might belong to. Spot-checks confirmed accurate transcription.
3. **EXACT-STRING-REUSE (18 groups) — trust as originally rated (STRONG).** Two different batches independently minted the identical working_label string. This is nearly always the SAME evolving research thread re-registering itself across adjacent batches (e.g. Step-291 kernel-operation-algebra-proposal across B0054/B0055) rather than coincidence — spot-checked and confirmed.
4. **SHARED-ALIAS (10 groups) — trust as originally rated (MODERATE).** Small, clean set; spot-checked and confirmed accurate.
5. **SHARED-NOTATION (144 groups) — DOWNGRADE further than the script's own note for short/generic codes; the script's own warning is correct and this pass found concrete confirming cases.** This agent flagged ~10 groups inline as ⚠ **likely noise**: bare 2-4 character sequential codes (`C-1`, `P4`, `T1..T8`, `F-1..F-5`, `D-1..D-10`, `A0..A6`, `I1..I10`, `P1..P10`, `F1..F10`) that recur as *independently-coined local numbering inside unrelated documents*, not as citations of one shared register — confirmed against `11-OBJECT-INDEX.jsonl` in the clearest cases (`C-1`, `C-1..C-12`). By contrast, longer/domain-specific notations (`INV-KOS-001`, `H-ZERO-001`, `GN-42`, `K_t=(A_t,R_t,E_t,H_t,Z_t,L_t)`) remain trustworthy signals of a real citation relationship. **One important non-noise exception is flagged explicitly (G0759, the `K_t` septuple-collision group): it is NOT noise — it is the mechanical fingerprint of a corpus-documented problem** (09-ORCHESTRATOR-FLAGS.md's B0037/B0069 findings that `K`/`𝕂`/`K_t` and other core symbols were independently rebound 7+ times). Read that group as evidence of the *problem*, never as an identity candidate.
6. **STRING-SIMILARITY (206 groups) — WEAK, and this pass found two opposite failure patterns worth distinguishing.** (a) ⚠ **Pure naming-convention noise**: groups whose only shared tokens are a generic scheme prefix/suffix with no topical connection — flagged inline in full for the `kr-<TOPIC>-2026-09-experiment` cluster (G1036-G1041: Access/Gödel/LL/Reiter are four unrelated experiments that merely share a dating convention). (b) 🔎 **Real-but-non-identity family membership**: the `kos-law-01..11` run (G0970-G1014) is NOT coincidental — these are 11 deliberately distinct ratified Articles of one Constitution — but grouping them by string similarity invites misreading "same family" as "merge candidate." Flagged inline at the first entry. P3 should expect both patterns to recur outside the specific groups annotated here; this agent pass sampled, it did not exhaustively adjudicate all 206 groups.
7. **CO-OCCURRENCE (832 groups) — WEAK, use only as a thematic-proximity index.** Sampled at both ends of the section (start and tail); the mechanical description ("co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] N times") was accurate in every sampled row. This section is the right place to look for *which threads run alongside which*, never for identity or even close relation on its own.

**Methodology note.** This is still a **candidate-grouping pass, not identity resolution.** The agent review below adds: (a) confirmation that a sample of the mechanical "why_grouped" claims accurately reflect the underlying ledger rows (spot-checked ~18 groups spanning all six signal types, zero transcription errors found), (b) explicit ⚠ noise flags on groups this agent assesses as coincidental collision (never deleted, per R5/R12 — annotated in place), and (c) a cross-reference against `09-ORCHESTRATOR-FLAGS.md`'s already-logged corpus-wide tensions, checking whether this mechanical pass caught or missed each one (see "Agent review notes" at the end of this file for the full account).

Interprets F_t=sigma(Y_1,...,Y_n) as the current information boundary, distinct from K_t, formally separating information accumulation (a filtration F_0 subset F_1 subset ...) from non-monotonic knowledge revision. Borrows Shum's innovation-process construction (Y_t=X_t-E[X_t|X_0,...,X_{t-1}]) to define 'new information' as observation content not already represented by the current information structure, and Shum's conditional-expectation-as-best-L2-estimator result to give a rigorous, non-truth-claiming interpretation of 'determination' (hat-X_t=E[X|F_t], with X-hat-X_t as the unresolved estimation residual, determination != truth). Splits the Knowledge Gap into an OPTIONAL probabilistic gap G_t^prob=D(Pi_t,Pi*) and a primary REQUIREMENT gap G_t^req={r in R_I : K_t does not sufficiently determine r}, with Zero(K_t,I_t,EC) iff G_t^req is empty -- explicitly preferred over trying to measure all knowledge with one probability distance. Uses push-forward measures to formalize joint/dependent dimensions D(X)=(d_1(X),...,d_n(X)) without assuming independence, and total-variation/coupling constructions to distinguish a probabilistic-distance layer Delta_prob from a still-unformalized semantic-distance layer Delta_semantic. Uses Shum's equality-almost-everywhere / convergence-in-distribution distinctions as further mathematical precedent for representation-equality != semantic-identity (K_t=K_{t+1} must never be inferred merely from an unchanged probabilistic representation). Produces an 11-layer unified research-level pipeline (World->Observation->Evidence->InformationStructure F_t->ProbabilisticRepresentation Pi_t (optional)->SemanticKnowledge K_t=Phi(F_t,E_t,Pi_t,S_t)->Zero->Determination->Decision->Governance->Action->new Observation) and narrows the entire remaining research programme to seven concrete named problems K1-K7, with K4 (constructing and proving the semantic map Phi: (F_t,E_t,Pi_t,S_t)->K_t) identified as 'the central KnowledgeOS mathematical problem' now that the surrounding mathematical substrate is judged substantially solved.
- **G0541** [`dretske-channel-information-knowledge-formalization` · `dretske-discriminate-semantic-selection-phi-decomposition`] — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'dretske-discriminate-semantic-selection-phi-decomposition' POSSIBLY relates to 'dretske-channel-information-knowledge-formalization' (batch B0056). Note: A revision of the earlier Dretske extraction after reading the book's later chapters (7-9, knowledge/belief/coding/cognitive structure/concepts), explicitly correcting the earlier chapters-1-5-only reading as incomplete. Central discovery: Dretske gives a candidate content for the previously-almost-empty semantic map Phi:(F_t,E_t,Pi_t,S_t)->K_t via information-bearing-structure -> selection/discrimination -> semantic content -> cognitive/functional state, since a physical/informational structure can carry many logically/nomically nested pieces of information (if F implies G, information(F) carries information(G)) while a cognitive system must discriminate among them and select one for higher-order treatment -- giving Entailed Information != Represented Knowledge as a knowledge-explosion-preventing principle, and grounding a candidate DISCRIMINATE operator Discriminate(I,RelevantAlternatives,Candidates)->SelectedContent. Finds Dretske's relevant-alternatives account of knowledge (knowledge = elimination of RELEVANT alternative possibilities, relevance depending on purposes/interests/context) structurally corresponds to KnowledgeOS's Zero(K,G,EC) as an eliminate-relevant-epistemic-gaps test (a correspondence hypothesis, not identity), and independently supports the Ideal State's context-dependence I_t(P,C). Establishes Information quantity != Semantic content != Knowledge quantity (a signal can carry a determinate amount of information without a determinate propositional content), reinforcing that K_t cannot be a scalar measure (K_t != H(X), K_t != P(X), K_t != bits). Decomposes Phi = Select o Discriminate o Interpret o Qualify o Represent and proposes a research hypothesis K_t = SemanticSelect(Information(F_t,E_t), I_t, EC), introducing a new intermediate layer I_t (script-I, selected semantic content) between the probabilistic representation Pi_t and K_t so that Pi_t never maps directly onto K_t. Cleanly divides remaining research labor: Kallenberg/Shum answer 'what information is available, how is uncertainty represented, how do variables depend'; Dretske answers 'what information is carried, what semantic content can be selected, which alternatives matter'; KnowledgeOS itself answers 'what knowledge state is constructed, is it sufficient, what should be decided/authorized.' Explicitly lists what Dretske does NOT solve (a formal K_t object, the atomic-claim schema, Sigma's four states, Governance, Authorization, Ideal-State representation, primitive minimality, software architecture), noting Dretske's own acknowledged restriction to empirical/perceptual knowledge with unresolved issues around necessary truths.
- **G0542** [`cover-thomas-sufficiency-distortion-formalization` · `shum-measure-theoretic-information-boundary-formalization`] — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'cover-thomas-sufficiency-distortion-formalization' POSSIBLY relates to 'shum-measure-theoretic-information-boundary-formalization' (batch B0056). Note: Extracts five results from Cover & Thomas relevant to unresolved KnowledgeOS questions (mutual information, the Data Processing Inequality, sufficient statistics, Fano's inequality, rate-distortion theory), explicitly not importing the whole communications-engineering book. Central move: uses the sufficient-statistic criterion I(theta;T(X))=I(theta;X) to argue K_t need not preserve ALL information from its source, only information relevant to its declared purpose (P,C) -- reframing the Ideal State I_t(P,C) from 'contains everything' to 'contains everything necessary for the declared purpose', and splitting Zero into a semantic-sufficiency test Suff(K_t,P,C) plus the pre-existing requirement-closure test G_t^req=empty. Uses the Data Processing Inequality (X->Y->Z implies I(X;Y)>=I(X;Z); no downstream processing can increase information about the original source) to state 'information creation != semantic derivation' and propose an anti-fabrication falsification test I(X;K_t)<=I(X;E_t) for purely downstream (e.g. LLM) transformations, while explicitly NOT prohibiting valid logical inference (derived knowledge != new empirical information). Uses Fano's inequality (residual uncertainty H(X|Y) lower-bounds unavoidable determination error) to distinguish exact determination (H(X|Y)=0) from approximate determination with a formally bounded error, rather than an ad hoc probability number. Uses rate-distortion theory (R(D)=min I(X,X-hat) subject to E[d(X,X-hat)]<=D) to reframe the KnowledgeOS design goal from 'maximum information' to 'minimum sufficient representation subject to acceptable epistemic loss' (K_t* = argmin Complexity(K) s.t. Distortion(K,I_t)<=D_acceptable and K sufficient for (P,C)) -- proposed as a candidate mathematical reformulation of the 'minimal kernel' question, replacing 'fewest primitive fields' with 'minimum representation preserving required epistemic semantics.' Introduces relevance-filtered dimension sets D_{P,C}(O) subset-of D(O) and a three-stage reduction (Information acquisition -> Relevant representation -> Knowledge construction), inserting a new intermediate layer R_t (relevant/sufficient semantic representation) between Pi_t and K_t. Corrects casual 'KL divergence as distance' language (D_KL is nonnegative and zero iff distributions agree but is not a true metric -- asymmetric, no triangle inequality -- so D_KL(Pi*||Pi_t) and D_KL(Pi_t||Pi*) are not interchangeable). Proposes a conditional-mutual-information novelty measure Delta I_t=I(X;E_{t+1}|F_t) to formalize 'new claim != new information != new knowledge' (a syntactically new claim k_4 can carry zero new information about the target if I(X;k_4|F_t)=0). Notes Kolmogorov complexity/the Kolmogorov sufficient statistic as a research-direction precedent for splitting K_t into (model/structure, residual evidence) rather than unrelated atomic claims. States the negative finding 'Information Theory != Knowledge Theory' (Cover & Thomas themselves say information is too broad to be captured by one definition), positioning Information Theory as a proper subset of the KnowledgeOS mathematical substrate where applicable. Distinguishes four kinds of change (information change F_t->F_{t+1}, probabilistic change Pi_t->Pi_{t+1}, semantic knowledge change K_t->K_{t+1}, and by extension decision/action change) as non-collapsing. Assembles a 14-layer unified pipeline (World/Observation/Evidence/InformationBoundary/ProbabilisticRepresentation/RelevantInformation/KnowledgeState/IdealState/Gap/Sufficiency/Determination/Decision/Authorization/Action) combining Kallenberg+Shum+Dretske+Cover-Thomas contributions.
- **G0543** [`complete-system-state-formalization` · `inquiry-first-class-object-and-smallest-adequate-answer`] — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'inquiry-first-class-object-and-smallest-adequate-answer' POSSIBLY relates to 'complete-system-state-formalization' (batch B0056). Note: Introduces Inquiry as a first-class KnowledgeOS object distinct from a linguistic question (Question subset-of Inquiry): Q=(T,P,C,R,Gamma) -- target, purpose, context, requirements, adequacy rules -- specifying an epistemic demand rather than a sentence. Reframes the whole system around a duality of bottom-up (World->Information->Knowledge) and top-down (Inquiry->Requirements->Investigation) directions, closing the loop Inquiry->RequiredKnowledge->Investigation->Knowledge->Answer. Makes the Ideal State INQUIRY-RELATIVE (Q->I_Q=IdealState(Q), not a free-floating construct) and refines Zero to Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC) meaning 'we know enough for THIS inquiry', not 'we know everything.' Defines a Smallest Adequate Answer A_Q*=argmin_{A in candidate-answers(Q,K_t)} Complexity(A) subject to Adequate(A,Q)=true, where Adequate is a conjunction of target/evidence/certainty/context/provenance/decision-condition satisfaction (predicate left as research work); explicitly separates two distinct minimization problems -- knowledge-representation minimization (K_t*) versus answer minimization (A_Q*), which can diverge arbitrarily (large K_t, tiny A_Q*). Establishes that the smallest adequate answer may legitimately be an epistemic negative (Determined/PartiallyDetermined/Undetermined/Conflicting/NotApplicable/Unknown), explicitly preferable to hallucinating a completion (worked example: a migration-feasibility inquiry with only firewall configuration missing should answer 'migration cannot yet be determined; missing firewall configuration', not 'yes'). Uses this to give Inquiry an investigation-control role (search only for gaps that affect THIS inquiry's answer, an inquiry-relative dimension-discovery objective d_Q*=argmax_d [adequacy-improvement-for-Q | investigate(d)]/Cost(d)) and a principled stopping condition (Stop iff Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC)=0), addressing the 'when does the system stop learning' problem. Distinguishes answer minimality as semantic (inquiry-determined relevance), not merely linguistic compression (a 500-word answer can be more minimal than a 20-word one that omits a required qualification). Connects to Dretske's semantic-selection chain (Information->SemanticContent->InquiryRelevance->Knowledge->Answer) and to Cover-Thomas's sufficiency/distortion apparatus (Inquiry->relevance->sufficiency->minimal representation) as the mathematical foundation for the compression step. Concludes with a five-line summary framing: Inquiry defines the destination; Knowledge State defines what has been established; Zero identifies what is missing; Investigation reduces the relevant gap; Answer is the minimal adequate projection of knowledge onto the inquiry. Possibly a re-derivation of the corpus's much earlier Inquiry-as-first-class-object proposals (inquiry-question-layer-refinement B0011, inquiry-context-doubt-to-settlement B0012, the Q_t component of complete-system-state-formalization B0019) rather than a genuinely new discovery -- not reconciled against those within this batch.
- **G0544** [`gita-three-level-translation-discipline` · `three-model-ten-convergences-and-four-non-convergences`] — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'three-model-ten-convergences-and-four-non-convergences' POSSIBLY relates to 'gita-three-level-translation-discipline' (batch B0056). Defines convergence at three levels distinct from the corpus's existing Gita-term/interpretation/construct translation discipline: Level 1 Structural (same relationship pattern appears independently), Level 2 Functional (different concepts play the same role, e.g. Buddhi and Discriminate/Qualify), Level 3 Formal (an actual structure-preserving map f:A->B with a relation-preserving reverse map -- the only level warranting the phrase 'mathematical correspondence'). Produces a 17-row correspondence table (World/Knower/Observation/Information/Uncertainty/Discrimination/RelevantContent/Knowledge/DesiredState/Gap/Determination/Choice/Authorization/Action/Feedback/Stability/Identity/UniversalKnower) across KnowledgeOS, Gita, and probability/information theory, explicitly marking several cells 'not native'/'not supplied' rather than force-filling them. States ten numbered convergences: (1) World!=Observation!=Representation!=Knowledge in all three (X!=Y_t!=Pi_t!=K_t; Kshetra!=Kshetrajna; signal!=extracted information); (2) knowledge/understanding is not a timeless static object; (3) information quantity != knowledge, and knowledge quantity != knowledge quality; (4) discrimination is central across all three (Buddhi; Dretske's content-selection; the corpus's own independently-introduced Discriminate operator; sufficient statistics/decoding); (5) knowledge/adequacy is always relative to a target/purpose (I_t(P,C); Dretske's relevant alternatives; a sufficient statistic being target-relative); (6) the system does not need everything -- knowledge = relevant and adequately discriminated understanding, not total information; (7) uncertainty is itself an epistemically meaningful state, not mere absence (paralleling the known/partial/uncertain/conflicting/unknown status vocabulary); (8) transformation E->K_t is potentially lossy, with loss acceptable iff adequacy is preserved; (9) the corpus's 'smallest adequate answer' A_Q* is a natural synthesis point where Cover-Thomas (minimal sufficient representation), Dretske (relevant semantic selection), Gita (discrimination) and KnowledgeOS structurally converge on the same design question without any one stating the equation; (10) the common object across all three is a knowledge-state TRANSITION SYSTEM (Inquiry->Observation->Information->Discrimination->Knowledge->Determination->Action->NewObservation), not a static knowledge database -- with a deeper shared theme that 'knowledge is evaluated relative to what is being sought' (Inquiry<->Purpose). Equally explicitly records four NON-convergences to avoid manufacturing agreement: (A) Atman (Gita's metaphysical persistent self) is NOT equivalent to the corpus's candidate persistent-identity abstraction script-I, and probability theory has no corresponding object at all; (B) Paramatma (Gita's universal knower) remains purely philosophical/metaphysical with no mathematical or KnowledgeOS counterpart required; (C) Dharma/Governance/Authorization is a KnowledgeOS-specific extension not obtainable from information theory, which has no authorization concept; (D) Gita supplies no (Omega,F,P) probability structure, so KnowledgeOS cannot define knowledge as probability on Gita's authority either -- probability remains a representation/measurement regime, not automatically the ontology of knowledge.

- **G0547** [`roopa-pai-vedas-upanishads-knowledge-hierarchy` · `vedic-implicit-information-theory-transmission-integrity`] — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'vedic-implicit-information-theory-transmission-integrity' POSSIBLY relates to 'roopa-pai-vedas-upanishads-knowledge-hierarchy' (batch B0056). Note: Extracts an implicit (non-Shannon) theory of information from the same Roopa Pai Vedas/Upanishads source's treatment of oral transmission, distinct from that file's knowledge-hierarchy extraction. Central claim: information is a representation transmissible between knowers but not identical with knowledge. Models the Vedic sound-based information carrier as multi-dimensional (words+pronunciation+rhythm+tone+emphasis+sequence, with Sama Veda melody notation as an encoding example), subject to transmission degradation (loss/distortion/addition/reinterpretation), for which the tradition's redundant multi-pattern recitation functioned as an error-detection/integrity mechanism (Original->multiple recitation Patterns A/B/C->cross-check->integrity). Enumerates five information channels (oral, musical, written, demonstrative, dialogical) noting the Upanishadic teacher-student form is INTERACTIVE (question-driven), not one-way broadcast. States the central distinction 'successful information transmission != successful knowledge transmission', splitting Information Transmission (Sender->Signal->Receiver) from Knowledge Transmission (Teacher->Signal->Student->Interpretation->Understanding->Experience->Realization). Adds a syntax/semantics/pragmatics decomposition of a signal, and states information is inherently contextual (Message+Context+Knower=Interpretation). Uses the historical example of ritual practice persisting after its meaning was lost (~700 BCE) as a concrete case of 'procedure preserved != purpose understood' (artifact integrity != semantic integrity), motivating a three-part integrity requirement: representation integrity (was what was said preserved), semantic integrity (was what it meant preserved), and intent integrity (was why it was said preserved). States information quality depends on the receiver, not just the message (World->Senses->Perception->Mind->Interpretation->Understanding, each stage introducing possible distortion), and that information is broader than language (linguistic/visual/auditory/behavioral/emotional/contextual/experiential), reformulated generally as 'information is a detectable difference that can alter the state of a receiver.' Concludes with a formal extracted definition ('information is a structured representation...carrying distinctions, meaning, or experience from a source to a receiver through a transmission channel; information becomes knowledge only when the receiver successfully integrates it into understanding') and a three-layer architecture (Information: representation/encoding/signal/storage/transmission/integrity -> Knowledge: meaning/context/understanding/validation/experience/reasoning -> Wisdom: judgment/action/transformation/capability/realization), plus four preserved principles: preserving information != preserving knowledge; preserving representation != preserving meaning; transmitting meaning != producing understanding; knowledge exists only when information has transformed the knower's capability.
- **G0548** [`epistemic-state-transition-object` · `rescorla-kernel-as-cognitive-mechanism-not-repository`] — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'rescorla-kernel-as-cognitive-mechanism-not-repository' POSSIBLY relates to 'epistemic-state-transition-object' (batch B0056). Reframes the central kernel question from 'is Buddhi the kernel' (rejected) to 'is the KnowledgeOS kernel a knowledge store or an epistemic cognitive mechanism' with the evidence favoring cognitive mechanism (K_t=state, script-K=transformation capability). Produces a 14-row kernel-capability test table (represent reality/maintain state/update state/combine prior+evidence/detect discrepancy/represent uncertainty/use context/have goals/select actions/revise beliefs: Yes or Likely with strong Rescorla evidence; produce knowledge/establish truth: NOT ESTABLISHED, Audi problem remains; governance/durable-organizational-storage: No, external layers). Gives the strongest current research-hypothesis equation K_{t+1}=script-K(K_t,E_t,Q_t,C_t) with probabilistic substructure Pi_{t+1} proportional-to Pi_t*L(E_t|H) while explicitly maintaining K_{t+1}!=Pi_{t+1}. This appears to be the direct originating mandate for the batch's own docs/knowledgeos/research/kernel-reduction/ file series (also read in this batch).
- **G0549** [`plato-object-knowledge-and-distinguish-requirement` · `plato-white-twelve-epistemological-principles`] — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'plato-object-knowledge-and-distinguish-requirement' POSSIBLY relates to 'plato-white-twelve-epistemological-principles' (batch B0056). Distinguishes propositional knowledge ('X is true') from object knowledge ('I understand X'), noting the Theaetetus's question is 'what does it mean for S to know X' not merely 'know that P' -- illustrated by a document asserting 'Nexus uses Podman' versus KnowledgeOS actually holding a validated multi-relational representation of Nexus (runtime/host/container/configuration/network/operational relationships). Extracts Plato's third logos-interpretation (knowing = being able to give a uniquely distinguishing description) as KNOW(X) requires DISTINGUISH(X, not-X), motivating Identity/Boundary/Distinction/Classification as KnowledgeOS capabilities, with a knowledge graph unable to reliably distinguish two entities framed as having an EPISTEMIC problem, not merely a data-quality one. Introduces 'epistemic contamination': Plato regards existing language/theory as potentially OBSTRUCTING correct apprehension of reality (OldModel->Bias->Misinterpretation->FalseKnowledge), proposed as a needed KnowledgeOS theory component. States inquiry is deliberate and question-driven (not random information collection) and itself RECURSIVE -- inquiry requires prior beliefs about what the question means, what counts as an answer, what terms mean, and what counts as relevant evidence, so K_t is used to search for K_{t+1} rather than starting from nothing. Adds a syntactic/semantic/epistemic correctness three-way non-collapse for representations. Closes with a 16-row Plato-contribution matrix and a final one-sentence summary: KnowledgeOS cannot equate information, representation, belief, truth, or consensus with knowledge; knowledge requires a reliable cognitive relation to objective reality supported by inquiry, distinction, definition and examination, with the exact final condition of knowledge left explicitly unresolved by Plato himself -- the unresolved '?' is characterized as deliberate and worth carrying into KnowledgeOS rather than resolving prematurely.

Defines a typed carrier-derivation table (ambient carriers: World/Context/Inquiry/IdealState/Policy/Rule/Objective/ActionSet/EpistemicState(K_t) -- none produced by any operator; derived carriers: Observation/SemanticContent/Representation/Evidence/Relation/Discrimination/Hypothesis/Claim/Defeater/Verdict/NormDelta/Gap/Determination/Decision) where a carrier kind is derived from (input-kind multiset, atoms introduced) rather than stamped by whichever operator produced it, formalizing Reach(S) as a monotone, terminating least fixpoint over ambient carriers -- deliberately excluding any hand-added 'obvious' closures or helper functions that could smuggle in a removed operator's work. Produces a 25-capability model (the protocol's C1-C24 plus a NEWLY ADDED C25 'admit an observation as evidence under a policy', justified because the corpus's Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence gap (G1) means C10's Verdict-requires-Evidence type rule is otherwise unrealizable -- an addition that makes minimization HARDER, not easier, so cannot be a convenience), with C18 (provenance) explicitly marked NON-DISCRIMINATING (structurally guaranteed by the reach engine's derivation-DAG bookkeeping, hence untestable by this instrument -- an explicit limitation of the instrument, not a finding about the kernel) and C20 (non-identifiability) operationalized with an explicit overreach failure mode (holding >=2 hypotheses plus returning UNDECIDED; failing by producing a Determination while unable to represent the alternatives). Computes an operator x capability matrix via actual leave-one-out removal-and-reevaluation (not asserted), yielding the experiment's headline empirical finding: Discriminate and DetectGap are BOTH ALL-ZERO ROWS under leave-one-out (neither is individually required for any capability, because each covers the other's shared atoms) -- explicitly NOT evidence the capabilities are unneeded but evidence the OPERATOR PACKAGING IS REDUNDANT; correspondingly C5 (discriminate alternatives) and C8 (detect epistemic insufficiency) are all-zero COLUMNS under leave-one-out and only become irreducible under PAIRWISE ablation (C5 lost only if {Discriminate,DetectGap} are BOTH removed, at the shared atom difference-decision; C8 lost if {Discriminate,DetectGap} or {DetectGap,Determine} are both removed, at difference-decision+norm-comparison) -- concluding a leave-one-out matrix alone would have wrongly declared C5/C8 unnecessary, which is the concrete justification for why pairwise ablation is mandatory and cardinality is only a secondary result. Confirms via the type system that Claim is producible ONLY via entailment (making its warrant kind DEDUCTIVE by construction, so a Verdict from generate-and-test is never a Claim, keeping 'Infer =?= Validate-compose-Hypothesize' a genuine open question rather than a definitional trick), that Verdict requires Evidence (making the corpus's absent Qualify function fatal to any C0-only realization), and that Determination requires BOTH NormDelta (hence IdealState) AND Inquiry (encoding the prior constraint that Ideal State is inquiry-relative). Formally distinguishes three notions of operator necessity that can and do disagree without being a defect -- empirically necessary (scenario/simulation fails without it), formally necessary (no valid composition of the rest supplies it via Reach), and DDD-necessary (a distinct domain responsibility) -- explicitly reporting they disagree for Select, Discriminate, and Revise. Rates per-operator corpus support from STRONG (Observe, Discriminate-as-a-family, Validate, Revise, Qualify) through MODERATE (Interpret, Infer, DetectGap, Challenge, Determine) to WEAK (Represent, Hypothesize, Select, Relate).

G0731/G0733 turned out to be genuine coincidental collisions (flagged ⚠ inline); G0734 is a real, trustworthy citation (`INV-KOS-001` used consistently by both labels for the same invariant); G0759 is real notation reuse that is itself a known corpus defect, not evidence of identity (flagged 🔎 inline, see above).

**Zero transcription/logic errors found** across all 18 spot-checks — the script's "why_grouped" text accurately reflects what is actually recorded in the ledger in every sampled case. This is a meaningfully positive finding about the script's reliability at the mechanical level; the concerns this review raises are about signal STRENGTH (generic-code collisions, naming-convention artifacts), not about the script mis-transcribing its inputs.

### Noise flagged

10 SHARED-NOTATION groups and 6 STRING-SIMILARITY groups (the `kr-*-2026-09-experiment` cluster) were flagged inline as ⚠ likely coincidental collision, all short/generic sequential codes (`C-1`, `C-1..C-12`, `P4`, `T1..T8`, `F-1..F-5`, `D-1..D-10`, `A0..A6`, `I1..I10`, `P1..P10`, `F1..F10`, and the `kr-<TOPIC>-2026-09-experiment` naming convention) reused independently across topically unrelated documents. This is a sample, not an exhaustive sweep of all 144 SHARED-NOTATION / 206 STRING-SIMILARITY groups — the same pattern almost certainly recurs elsewhere in both sections (e.g. most of the un-annotated `G1..G5`/`L1..L5`/`A1..A10`-style entries deserve the same scrutiny in P2b/P3); this pass prioritized breadth across signal types over exhaustive coverage of any one section, consistent with the task's spot-check mandate. Two groups were flagged in the opposite direction (🔎 real-but-non-identity family membership, not noise): G0759 (`K_t`, a known symbol-overload defect) and G0970 (`kos-law-0X`, a real 11-Article enumeration) — both risk being misread as merge candidates precisely because they are NOT random noise.

### Cross-reference against `09-ORCHESTRATOR-FLAGS.md`'s known tensions

| Known tension (batch) | Caught by mechanical clustering? |
|---|---|
| K/𝕂/K glyph collision, 7 definitions (B0069) | **CAUGHT** — G0759 (SHARED-NOTATION, `K_t` shared by exactly 7 labels) is a precise mechanical fingerprint of this exact finding. Annotated 🔎 in place. |
| Competing minimal-kernel-size figures: 14 (B0043), 13/8 (B0057), 49-incompatible-enumerations (B0062) | **MOSTLY MISSED.** Searched the draft for `s1612-k-minimality`, `kos-minimal-kernel`, `k-min-capability-basis-apparatus`, `kmin-stipulated-not-derived`, `ocore-necessity-proof-gap`, `forced-operation`/`lower-bound` labels: these form several SEPARATE small POSSIBLY-RELATION/SHARED-NOTATION clusters (e.g. G0217, G0840, G0841) that do **not** mechanically converge into one group, because each batch used different variable names/symbols for its own "minimal kernel" claim. The specific 14/13/8/49 figures never appear together in any one group. **This is exactly the kind of case the mandate anticipated**: the mechanical pass cannot connect claims that are the same underlying dispute but use disjoint vocabulary — P2b/P3 will need to manually construct a "minimal-kernel-size" object family from the orchestrator-flags narrative, not from this file's groups. |

Consistent with, and a mechanical corroboration of, the corpus's own repeatedly-self-diagnosed Zero-naming proliferation. |

No POSSIBLY-RELATION, SHARED-NOTATION, or STRING-SIMILARITY signal connects the v1.0/v1.1/v1.2 labels as a lineage. P3 will need to reconstruct this lineage narratively from the orchestrator flags, not from this file's stronger signal types. |
| Gita-lane vs. disciplined-lane split (B0048-B0062, the corpus's most-repeated structural finding) | **MISSED.** This is a narrative/behavioral pattern (two research lanes reaching opposite conclusions from the same underlying material on the same day) rather than a label-similarity pattern, so it does not manifest as shared notation/alias/string overlap between the specific competing documents. Only one incidental CO-OCCURRENCE tie was found (G1901, `glyph-register-v3-collision-inventory-2026-09` / `lane-conflict-v4-evidence-package-H2-2026-09`) and it does not capture the pattern itself. **This is a genuine, structural miss**: no amount of P2b re-grouping by label signal will surface the Lane-A/Lane-B split — it has to be carried forward as a standing methodological caution (already well-documented in 09-ORCHESTRATOR-FLAGS.md) rather than as an object family. |
| "Governance-ratification-claims-are-unreliable" (B0062's two-independent-audit finding) | **MISSED** at the grouping level for the same reason as the Gita-lane split — it is a verdict about a whole class of self-declared `[RATIFIED]` claims, not a pairwise label relationship. Individual self-attested-ratification objects do appear in POSSIBLY-RELATION/UNKNOWN-CANDIDATE-GROUP entries (e.g. G0704, G0706 on self-attested "HPA" verdicts) but nothing ties them together as instances of the B0062 finding. |

**Overall pattern**: the mechanical pass is reliable and non-error-prone at the level of individual group claims (0 transcription errors in 18 spot-checks), and it correctly surfaces tensions that manifest as **shared vocabulary** (the K_t collision). It structurally cannot surface tensions that are **narrative/behavioral** (Lane-A/Lane-B splits, ratification unreliability) or that involve **disjoint vocabulary describing the same dispute** (the competing minimal-kernel-size figures). These three categories of miss are not defects in the script — they are outside what label-similarity clustering can detect in principle — and should be treated by P2b/P3 as a standing worklist item to reconstruct manually from `09-ORCHESTRATOR-FLAGS.md` rather than expected to fall out of further label-normalization tooling.

### Recommendations for P2b/P3 priority, beyond the existing "most cross-referenced" table

- **Build a "minimal-kernel-size" object family manually in P2b.** The 14 (B0043) / 13-or-8 (B0057) / 49-incompatible-enumerations (B0062) figures, plus `s1612-k-minimality-proof-and-valid-k-computability`, `kos-minimal-kernel`, `kos-primitive-reduction-kernel`, `k-min-capability-basis-apparatus`, `kmin-stipulated-not-derived`, and `ocore-necessity-proof-gap`, are almost certainly members of one long-running dispute that this mechanical pass could not connect. High priority given B0064's finding that "count the operators" may be the wrong kind of measurement entirely.
- **Build a "v1.0→v1.2 theory-version lineage" object family manually.** Same reasoning as above; CO-OCCURRENCE alone is too weak a trace for something this load-bearing (B0057's proven impossibility theorem, B0058's "semantically incoherent" verdict).
- **Treat the Gita-lane/disciplined-lane split and the governance-ratification-unreliability finding as standing cross-cutting cautions carried forward from Phase 1, not as candidates for label-family construction** — P3 should consult `09-ORCHESTRATOR-FLAGS.md` directly for these rather than expecting P2b's object families to encode them.
- **The Zero/Śūnya family (36 labels, ~10 fragmented sub-groups) deserves a dedicated P2b write-up** even though this pass could not unify it mechanically — it is exactly the kind of large, semantically-coherent-but-lexically-fragmented family that a human/agent object-family pass (not a string-matching script) is suited to reconstruct.
- **A second pass over the un-annotated SHARED-NOTATION/STRING-SIMILARITY entries** (this review sampled roughly 20 of 144+206) should apply the same generic-code skepticism developed here — candidates like the several remaining `G1..Gn`/`L1..Ln`-style bare codes not yet reviewed.
